name: When Steam Ruled the Rails
description: How coal, iron and a kettle that learned to pull turned slow roads into railways, and what came after the steam locomotive.

checkpoints.name: Before the rails
checkpoints.note: Coaches and wagons crawl along muddy roads while Newcomen and Watt teach steam to pump and turn. A steam wagon in France shows that an engine can move itself, if slowly.

checkpoints.name: The first iron roads
checkpoints.note: Stephenson's Locomotion and Rocket prove that steam locomotives can carry people and goods. Cities build tram lines and the first underground, and America links its coasts by rail in 1869.

checkpoints.name: Empires of steel
checkpoints.note: Cheap steel lets railways cross continents. The Trans-Siberian and the Orient Express become romantic journeys, and the Mallard sets a speed record for steam in 1938.

checkpoints.name: Speed reborn
checkpoints.note: Diesel and electric trains replace steam. Japan opens the Shinkansen in 1964, France follows with the TGV, and China runs a magnetic levitation line at over four hundred kilometres per hour.
